name: IEC shift register (SRGm)
summary: IEC register marked SRGm with m stages; the clock carries the shift arrow and moves data one place each cycle.
description: SRGm identifies a shift register of m bits. The clock input is labelled with C1 and a shift arrow, showing that each active edge moves data one place. The serial input is labelled 1D, and the parallel outputs are listed down the right side, typically in a column of per-bit elements under a common-control block.

On drawings, shift registers expand outputs for indicators or relay drivers, or capture serial data from a sensor. The reader should identify the shift direction, the serial input, and any output latch or enable, as these decide how and when outputs update.
The symbol does not show the data rate or the serial protocol. Those come from the controller documentation driving the register.
readingNotes: Identify the shift direction from the arrow.
Check for an output latch that holds outputs during shifting.
drawingChecklist: State the bit count in the qualifier.
Show the output latch and enable if present.
distinction: A latched shift register adds a storage register and its own clock between the shift stages and the outputs.
